shots.purpose: Open on the paradox: an ocean of brown desert cut by a green ridge strip with fog pressing in
shots.claim: green vegetation patches survive on Atacama ridgelines without rain
shots.evidence: terrain-field plate: brown desert field, dark ocean edge, thin green ridge dashes, soft fog wash from the coast
shots.motion_reason: slow push toward the green strip so the desert-versus-garden mismatch reads at once

depth.note: fog plane over ridge over desert reconstructs the coastal cross-section in map form

subject_contract.expected_subject: map plate: brown desert, dark ocean edge, green ridge strip, incoming fog wash

one_second.relationship: fog crawls toward a garden that should not exist

shots.purpose: Establish the dryness number and the two failing moisture sources
shots.claim: the Atacama's core averages under 1 millimetre of rain per year
shots.evidence: map zoom with blocked arrows: Andes wall east, cold current west, both moisture paths dead-ended
shots.motion_reason: contract from region to the desert core while the two arrows are cut off

depth.note: blocked arrows annotate the geography; the number chip carries the key figure

subject_contract.expected_subject: map plate: Atacama core with two blocked moisture arrows and a 1 MM/YEAR chip

one_second.relationship: two moisture sources surround the desert and both fail

shots.purpose: Reveal the lomas ribbons on the map inside the 300-1000 m band
shots.claim: fog oases called lomas form green ribbons on coastal ridgelines between roughly 300 and 1,000 metres
shots.evidence: map reveal: brown field cut by thin green ribbons along ridgelines, elevation band chip
shots.motion_reason: hold steady while ribbons light up; a small zoom keeps the map readable

depth.note: ribbons are content drawn in the art, revealed by state changes

subject_contract.expected_subject: map plate: brown desert with green lomas ribbons and a 300-1000 M chip

one_second.relationship: hidden gardens appear exactly on ridgelines

shots.purpose: Explain the camanchaca: cold current fog deck under a warm lid, pierced by ridges
shots.claim: the camanchaca is a coastal fog deck formed over the cold Humboldt Current and capped by a warm-air inversion
shots.evidence: cross-section: ocean, cold current band, fog deck, warm lid line, ridge spearing through with droplets on leaves
shots.motion_reason: slow traverse along the cross-section from ocean to ridge as the mechanism assembles
shots.transition_reason: cut to the mesh yield number

depth.note: the deck-under-lid stack is the mechanism; the ridge is the failure point of the lid

subject_contract.expected_subject: cross-section plate: ocean, fog deck under warm lid, ridge piercing the deck

one_second.relationship: the ridge pierces the lid-capped fog deck and collects its water

shots.purpose: Quantify the yield: mesh panels harvest 2-5 litres per square metre per day
shots.claim: standard fog collectors in prime fog zones harvest roughly 2 to 5 litres per square metre per day
shots.evidence: mesh panel with droplets and drip line into a tank beside a leaf doing the same trick; yield chip
shots.motion_reason: push toward the dripping mesh while droplets count into the tank

depth.note: droplet-to-tank flow gives the number a physical source

subject_contract.expected_subject: plate: fog mesh panel dripping into a tank with a 2–5 L chip

one_second.relationship: mesh turns fog into litres of water

shots.purpose: Scale the mechanism: village arrays plus the Mars-analog twist
shots.claim: village-scale fog arrays deliver hundreds of litres per day and NASA tests Mars instruments in the Yungay core
shots.evidence: stacked mesh walls feeding tanks with a pipe run, and a Mars-analog flag pinned on the desert core
shots.motion_reason: pan across the array, then settle on the Mars-analog pin

depth.note: the array is the lomas copied in steel and mesh

subject_contract.expected_subject: plate: village fog array with tanks plus a MARS ANALOG pin

one_second.relationship: the same trick, engineered at village scale in the most Mars-like place on Earth

shots.purpose: Resolve the rule: rain never comes — the ocean delivers water sideways as fog, and ridges catch it
shots.claim: the Atacama's hidden water source is sideways ocean fog that only ridgelines can catch
shots.evidence: resolved map: fog arrows running sideways from ocean to ridges, gardens blooming exactly where the arrows land
shots.motion_reason: slow pull back so the whole sideways-water map resolves in one frame

depth.note: the full map logic resolves: no rain, sideways water, ridges as taps

subject_contract.expected_subject: resolved map plate: sideways fog arrows onto blooming ridgelines

one_second.relationship: the desert's water walks, it never falls
